name: grad_zero
summary: Zero-fill tensor (typically gradients). Writes Y = 0 for f16/f32 contiguous tensors of any rank using cudaMemsetAsync. Supports in-place (X and Y may alias).
contract: - X and Y same rank and same shape
- In-place allowed (X.data may equal Y.data). Input is not read; only output is written.
- Y is filled with zeros (byte-wise memset to 0). For f16/f32, this corresponds to numeric 0.
notes: dtype_bytes: f32=4 bytes, f16=2 bytes; other dtypes rejected.
numel_anyrank(): returns 0 if rank<=0 or any dim<=0; otherwise product(shape).
Launcher clears previous CUDA error with cudaGetLastError() before memset and returns last error after.
Because this is memset-based, performance is typically bandwidth-bound and launch overhead dominates for small tensors.

variants.name: grad_zero
supported: X,Y same rank and same shape
notes: Backend op is a cudaMemsetAsync (not a custom kernel).
If n==0 => return Ok without launching memset.

experiments.title: Fuse grad_zero into optimizer step
experiments.change: Remove standalone grad_zero op; perform gradient zeroing inside fused optimizer kernel after consuming grad.
experiments.why: Standalone memset adds an extra dispatch; fusion can reduce launch count and improve small-model step latency.
experiments.hypothesis: Lower end-to-end optimizer step time when many parameters are small tensors.
experiments.proof: nsys launch count and step timing; ensure gradients are zeroed at correct point in training loop.
experiments.next: Add a flag to keep standalone op for debugging/repro flows.

experiments.title: Compare cudaMemsetAsync vs custom vectorized kernel
experiments.change: Implement a vectorized zero kernel (e.g., int4 stores) and compare with cudaMemsetAsync across sizes.
experiments.why: cudaMemsetAsync is usually fast, but a custom kernel may win in some graph-capture or alignment scenarios.
experiments.hypothesis: For very large tensors, both are bandwidth-bound; for mid sizes, custom kernel might reduce overhead or improve scheduling.
experiments.proof: Benchmark latency and achieved bandwidth; confirm correctness.
experiments.next: If custom kernel wins, gate on alignment and size; otherwise keep memset.

measurements.notes: Zero-fill is memory-bound; effective bytes written = n * dtype_bytes. GB/s is meaningful; TFLOP/s not meaningful.
